title: Session Locksmith - mini PRD for deterministic session unlocks
content:
Context / why I care:
- We have lots of heuristics for session restoration, mem/caching, and KV expiration. They work fine, but product teams keep asking for "deterministic unlocks" — i.e., a way to take a cold session and reliably rehydrate only the tokens/anchors needed for a specific task (search, summarization, chat continuity) without paying for full prefix restore.

Problem statement (short):
- Users want predictable latency/cost when resuming long conversations or switching tasks inside a session. Current 'restore everything' model is expensive and noisy.

Goals:
- Define a lightweight session-unlock API that returns a compact payload sufficient for a particular task (task-scoped context).
- Make restore deterministic and idempotent: same request = same minimal payload + cost estimate.
- Integrate with existing KV/prefix cache so we reuse warm caches when available.

Non-goals:
- Not a replacement for full session playback (we keep that).
- Not designing UI; this is API + server behavior.

Proposed API (sketch):
POST /v1/sessions/{id}/unlock
body: {"intent": "summary|search|chat", "max_context_tokens": 1024, "fidelity_budget": "low|medium|high", "anchors": ["user-bio","last-3-turns"]}
response: {"payload_id": "uuid", "tokens_estimated": 312, "kv_reads": 4, "compact_context": "base64...", "fallbacks": ["full_restore_allowed"]}

User stories:
- As a dev, I want to request an unlock for intent=search and get back a compact context to pass to the model, so my search route stays sub-200ms most of the time.
- As a platform engineer, I want a predictable cost estimate for unlocks so I can surface billing in the console and gate heavy restores.
- As a product PM, I want to roll out a canary that maps low-fidelity unlocks to fallback full restores if results degrade.

Acceptance criteria (rough):
- API returns payload <= configured token budget 95% of the time for sampled sessions.
- Cost estimate error <= 20% for p95.
- Integrates with KV cache: if KV cache contains anchors, unlock latency < 100ms (p90) in a single-region config.

Data/model behavior notes:
- Unlock logic will run a lightweight scorer over session meta: importance-weighted recent tokens, named anchors, and static user-profile hints.
- We should consider a tiny distilled reranker (CPU-bound) to pick anchors.
- Fall back to: pin last-3-turns or full restore depending on fidelity_budget.

Implementation sketch / infra impact:
- New endpoint + unlock service that queries KV index and session index.
- Cache warm-path: if session is hot on GPU, return pointer to warmed KV slice instead of copying tokens.
- Budgeting: unlock should produce a cost estimate using same tokenization and model-matching rules as billing.

Metrics to track:
- Unlock latency (p50/p90/p99), cost_estimate vs actual cost, success rate (payload fits budget), downstream model quality delta (A/B against full restore).

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Internal alpha: support intent=chat|search; log-only cost estimates; small subset of internal traffic.
2) Beta: allow fidelity_budget toggles, console surfacing for cost estimates; opt-in for customers.
3) GA: SDK helpers + server-side canary rules.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to represent "anchors" schema standardly? freeform tags vs typed anchors? (ask Mira)
- Should unlock be synchronous always, or support async payload-building for expensive sessions?
- Evaluate privacy/legal: do compact_context payloads need additional redaction? (Hanae to check)
- Performance cost of small reranker: CPU vs tiny GPU (benchmark with 10k sessions).

Notes to self / next actions:
- Prototype scorer in Python notebook using existing session export (use JIRA-INF-948 dataset).
- Sync with infra about adding payload_id + short-lived object storage for compact_contexts.
- Draft console mockups to show cost estimate and fidelity slider.

Random brain-things:
- Could treat "unlock" as a reversible transform: canonicalize + delta; store delta small. Enables cheap diffs between intents.
- Maybe add "preferred_model_family" as a hint so unlock picks tokens that matter for that model (e.g., long-context vs standard).

End of scratchpad. Keep terse — this will become PRD seed for 2025 Q2 feature exploration.
